They were narrated by the trustworthy imams, meaning: do not say 'So-and-so is better than so-and-so,' nor 'So-and-so is more excellent than so-and-so.'" [End of quotation.]

Ibn Kathir said, in answer to this difficulty, the following text: "The answer is from several aspects. One: that this was before it was made known that there is preference. In this there is scrutiny.

Two: that he said this out of humility and modesty.

Three: that this is a prohibition of preference in such a situation, where they were brought to judgment during a quarrel and dispute.

Four: do not prefer by mere opinion and partisanship.

Five: the station of preference is not up to you; it is to Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, and upon you is submission, surrender to Him, and belief in Him." [End of quotation, in its own words.]

Al-Qurtubi mentioned in his *Tafsir* many answers to this difficulty. He chose that the prohibition of preference applies specifically to prophethood, while preference in other matters is permissible — such as increases in states, special distinctions, miracles, and noble gifts. For he said the following text: "I say: better than this is the statement of one who said: The prohibition of preference is only with respect to prophethood itself, which is one quality in which there is no differing, whereas preference is in increases of states, special distinctions, noble gifts, subtle favors, and differing miracles.

As for prophethood in itself, it is not subject to greater or lesser degrees. Rather, distinction is by other matters added to it. For this reason, some of them are messengers and possessors of firm resolve (*Ulul-'Azm*), some of them were taken as an intimate friend, and some of them Allah spoke to, and He raised some of them in rank. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We have certainly caused some of the prophets to exceed others, and to Dawud We gave the Zabur﴾ [17]. I say: This is a good view, for it reconciles the verses and the hadiths without abrogation (*naskh*, i.e., the replacement of one ruling by a later one). The statement that some are preferred over others is only by what He granted of virtues and bestowed of means. Ibn 'Abbas has indicated this when he said: 'Allah preferred Muhammad (ﷺ) over the prophets and over the people of heaven.' They said: 'By what, O Ibn 'Abbas, did He prefer him over the people of heaven?' He said: 'Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him," then We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 29], and He said to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest, that Allah may forgive you your past sin and what will follow﴾ [48].' They said: 'What is his preference over the prophets?' He said: 'Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except in the language of his people, to make clear for them﴾ [Ibrahim: 4], and Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, said to Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾ [Saba': 28]. So He sent him to the jinn and mankind.' This was mentioned by Abu Muhammad al-Darimi in his *Musnad*. And Abu Hurayrah said: 'The best of the children of Adam are Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Muhammad (ﷺ), and they are the possessors of firm resolve among the messengers.' This is an explicit statement from Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Hurayrah in specifying them. And it is known that whoever is sent is better than whoever is not sent, for whoever is sent is distinguished over others by the messengership, and they are equal in prophethood. As for what the messengers encounter of the denial of their peoples and their killing of them, this is something not hidden." [End of quotation, the relevant portion, in its own words.]

Ibn 'Atiyyah chose, as al-Qurtubi transmitted from him, that the way of reconciliation is the permissibility of preference in general terms, as in His saying (ﷺ): "I am the master of the children of Adam, and I say this without boasting," without specifying. And he prohibited preference in a particular manner, as in His saying: "Do not prefer me over Musa," and His saying: "It is not befitting for anyone to say, 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta,'" and similar. And Allah knows best.

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and then do not follow what they have spent with reminder or injury — for them is their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾ It is understood from this verse that whoever follows his charity with reminder and injury does not obtain this reward mentioned here, in His saying: ﴿with reminder or injury, for them is their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 262]. And He has explicitly stated this understanding in (p-158) His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not nullify your charities with reminder and injury﴾ — the verse [Al-Baqarah: 264].

Author's introduction in (Dafʿ Iham al-Idtirab ʿan Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion; the right course has become clear from the wrong.﴾

This verse, on its apparent meaning, indicates that no one is to be compelled to enter the religion. A parallel to it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Would you then compel the people until they become believers?﴾ [Yunus: 99].

(p-227) And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We did not send you as a guardian over them; your duty is only to convey [the message]﴾ [al-Shura: 48]. Yet there occur in many verses things that indicate the compulsion of disbelievers to enter Islam by the sword, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You will fight them, or they will submit﴾ [al-Fath: 16], and His saying: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 193], meaning shirk.

This interpretation is supported by the sound hadith: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no god but Allah," and so on. The answer to this is given in two ways:

The first, which is the more correct: this verse is specific to the People of the Book. The meaning is that before the revelation of their fighting, they were not compelled in religion at all, and after the revelation of their fighting, they are not compelled to it when they give the jizyah (poll-tax) willingly ("ʿan yadin," i.e., in submission) and they are humbled (wa-hum saghirun).

The evidence that it is specific to them is what Abu Dawud, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban and Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "A woman would be a muqlat (one whose children do not survive), so she would vow that if a child lived for her, she would make him a Jew. When the Banu al-Nadir were expelled, there were among them sons of the Ansar, and they said: 'We will not leave our sons.' So Allah revealed: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion.﴾"

Al-muqlat: she whose child does not survive. And in the proverb: "More burning than the tears of the muqlat."

Ibn Jarir also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾ was revealed concerning a man of the Ansar from the Banu Salim ibn ʿAwf called al-Husayn. He had two Christian sons, while he himself was a Muslim. He said to the Prophet: 'Shall I not compel them, for they have refused anything but Christianity?' So Allah revealed the verse."

Ibn Jarir also related that Saʿid ibn Jubayr was asked by Abu Bishr about this verse, and he said: "It was revealed concerning the Ansar." He asked: "Specifically?" He said: "Specifically."

Ibn Jarir also narrated from Qatadah by two chains concerning His saying: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾, that he said: "This tribe of the Arabs was compelled to it, because they were an unlettered nation having no book they knew, so nothing but Islam was accepted from them. But the People of the Book are not compelled to it when they consent to the jizyah or the kharaj and are not turned away from their religion, so they are left alone."

Ibn Jarir also narrated from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾, or he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to fight the people of idolatry in the Arabian Peninsula, and nothing was accepted from them except "There is no god but Allah" or the sword. Then he was commanded concerning others than them to accept the jizyah from them, so He said: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion; the right course has become clear from the wrong.﴾

Ibn Jarir also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, again, concerning His saying: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion﴾, he said: "That was when people entered Islam and the People of the Book gave the jizyah."

These reports indicate that it is specific to the People of the Book who give the jizyah and those who are in their ruling. This is not refuted by the principle that the lesson lies in the generality of the wording and not in the specificity of the occasion of revelation, because the specification here is known through transmission from the scholars of tafsir, not merely from the specificity of the occasion. Among what indicates the specificity is what is established in the Sahih: "Your Lord marvels at a people who are led into Paradise in chains."

The second answer: it has been abrogated (mansukhah) by the verses of fighting, such as His saying: ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5], and the verse. It is known that Surat al-Baqarah was among the first revealed at Madinah, while Surat Bara'ah was among the last revealed there. The view of abrogation is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and Zayd ibn Aslam. In any case, the verses of the sword were revealed after the surah containing: ﴿There is no compulsion﴾, and the later takes precedence over the earlier. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 257:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah is the Walī (Protector and Ally) of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257]. In this noble verse He explicitly states that Allah is the Walī of the believers. In another verse He states that He is their Walī, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is their Walī, and that some of them are Awliyā' (allies) of others. This is in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Your Walī is only Allah and His Messenger and those who believe﴾ [al-Mā'idah: 55], and His saying: ﴿The believing men and believing women are Awliyā' of one another﴾ [al-Tawbah: 71]. In another place He explicitly restricts this walāyah (protection and alliance) to the Muslims, excluding the disbelievers, in His saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the Mawlā (Protector) of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no Mawlā﴾ [Muhammad: 11]. In another place He states that His Prophet (ﷺ) has more right over the believers than they have over themselves, in His saying: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 6]. In this verse of al-Baqarah He clarifies the fruit of His walāyah toward the believers, which is bringing them out of darkness into light, in His saying: ﴿Allah is the Walī of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257]. In another place He clarifies that among the fruits of His walāyah is the removal of fear and grief from His Awliyā', and that their walāyah toward Him is by their faith and piety. This is in His saying: ﴿Surely the Awliyā' of Allah—there is no fear for them, nor do they grieve; those who believe and used to be mindful of Allah﴾ [Yūnus: 62–63]. In another place He states that He is the Walī of His Prophet (ﷺ), and that He also takes charge of the righteous, in His saying: ﴿Surely my Walī is Allah, who sent down the Book, and He takes charge of the righteous﴾ [al-A'rāf: 196].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He brings them out of darkness into light﴾. The meaning of "darkness" (al-ẓulumāt) is misguidance (al-ḍalālah), and the meaning of "light" (al-nūr) is guidance (al-hudā). From this verse it is understood that the paths of misguidance are many, as shown by His use of the plural "darknesses" (al-ẓulumāt), while the path of truth is one, as shown by His use of the singular "light" (al-nūr). This meaning indicated here He clarified in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they scatter you away from His way﴾ [al-An'ām: 153].

Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir of this verse, and its text is: "For this reason He made the word 'light' singular and the 'darknesses' plural, because the truth is one, while disbelief has many kinds, and all of them are false, as He said: ﴿And that this is My path, straight, so follow it, and do not follow other ways, lest they scatter you away from His way. That He has enjoined you with, that you may be mindful of Allah﴾ [al-An'ām: 153]. He also said: ﴿and made the darknesses and the light﴾ [al-An'ām: 1], and He said: ﴿on the right and on the left, in separate groups﴾ [al-Ma'ārij: 37], and other verses whose wording conveys that the truth is singular, while falsehood spreads, multiplies, and branches out in its wording." (p. 159)

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, their Awliyā' are the Ṭāghūt (false deities/transgressors)﴾, to the end of the verse. Some scholars said: the ṭāghūt (everything worshipped besides Allah, a term for any object of false worship or transgressing authority) is Satan. What supports this is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is only Satan, who frightens you of his Awliyā'﴾ [Āl 'Imrān: 175], meaning he frightens you of his allies. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe fight in the way of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the way of the Ṭāghūt, so fight the Awliyā' of Satan; surely the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾ [al-Nisā': 76]. And His saying: ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as Awliyā' besides Me, while they are an enemy to you?﴾ [al-Kahf: 50]. And His saying: ﴿They have taken the devils as Awliyā'﴾ [al-A'rāf: 30]. The verified position is that everything worshipped besides Allah is ṭāghūt, and the greatest share of that belongs to Satan, as He said: ﴿Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan?﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 60]. He also said: ﴿They invoke besides Him only females, and they invoke only a rebellious devil﴾ [al-Nisā': 117]. He said, concerning His close friend Ibrahim: ﴿O my father, do not worship Satan﴾ [Maryam: 44]. And He said: ﴿Surely the devils inspire their Awliyā' to dispute with you; and if you obey them, you are surely polytheists﴾ [al-An'ām: 121]. And other verses besides these.

Allah's words: ﴿Like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people﴾. He made clear that what is meant by "the one" (alladhi) is "those" (alladhina), by His words: ﴿they have no power over anything they have earned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 264].

Allah's saying: ﴿For the poor who have been confined in the way of Allah﴾ and so on [al-Baqarah: 273]. He does not explain here the cause of their poverty, but He explains in Surah al-Hashr that the cause of their poverty is the expulsion of the disbelievers from their homes and their wealth, in His saying: ﴿For the poor emigrants who have been driven out from their homes and their wealth﴾ and so on [al-Hashr: 8].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 275:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists, for him is what has passed﴾ — the verse.

The meaning of this noble verse is that whoever receives an admonition from his Lord that restrains him from consuming usury (riba), and desists, i.e., abandons dealing in riba out of fear of Allah, the Exalted, and in compliance with His command, "for him is what has passed," i.e., what passed before the revelation of the prohibition of riba-money. From this noble verse it is derived that Allah does not hold a person accountable for doing a matter except after He has made it unlawful for him. He clarified this meaning in many verses. He said concerning those who used to drink wine and consume the wealth of gambling (maysir) before the prohibition was revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾ — the verse [al-Ma'idah: 93].

(p-160) And He said concerning those who used to marry the wives of their fathers before the prohibition: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed﴾ [an-Nisa': 22], i.e., but what passed before the prohibition, there is no blame upon you for it. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And that you take in marriage two sisters simultaneously, except what has already passed﴾ — the verse [an-Nisa': 23].

And He said concerning hunting before the prohibition: ﴿Allah has pardoned what has passed﴾ — the verse [al-Ma'idah: 95].

And He said concerning prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis before the abrogation of facing it: ﴿And Allah would not have let your faith (iman) be lost﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143], i.e., your prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis before the abrogation.

And among the clearest evidences for this meaning is that when the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims asked forgiveness for their dead relatives among the polytheists, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ [at-Tawbah: 113], and they regretted their asking forgiveness for the polytheists, Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿And Allah would not misguide a people after He has guided them until He has made clear to them what they should beware of﴾ [at-Tawbah: 115]. Thus He declared that He does not misguide them by doing a matter except after making clear to them what to avoid.

**Section on Riba (Usury)**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿God destroys usury﴾. In this noble verse He states explicitly that He destroys usury, meaning He removes it entirely from the hand of its possessor, or deprives it of blessing, so that he derives no benefit from it, as Ibn Kathir and others have said. What is mentioned here regarding the destruction of usury is indicated in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And whatever you give in usury so that it may increase within the wealth of people, it does not increase with God﴾ [al-Rum: 39], and His saying: ﴿Say: The bad and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of the bad impresses you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 100], and His saying: ﴿And He will place the bad upon one another, heap it all together, and place it in Hell﴾. Ibn Kathir also pointed to this in his commentary on this verse.

Know that God explicitly prohibited usury in His saying: ﴿And God has made trade lawful and has forbidden usury﴾ [al-Baqarah: 275]. He also explicitly stated that one who deals in usury is at war with God, in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of usury, if you are believers. And if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger. But if you repent, you will have your principal; you will not wrong and you will not be wronged﴾ [al-Baqarah: 278–279].

He also stated that the consumer of usury will not rise, i.e., from his grave on the Day of Resurrection, except as one rises whom Satan has struck with madness, in His saying: ﴿Those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say: Trade is only like usury﴾ [al-Baqarah: 275]. (p-161) The hadiths on this are very numerous.

Know that among usury is that upon whose prohibition the Muslims have agreed, and no one has differed concerning it. This is like the usury of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era), which is that one increases the term of the debt in exchange for the other increasing the amount of the debt. And there is riba al-nasa' (usury of delay) in gold for gold, silver for silver, gold for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, and salt for salt, and likewise among these four types with one another.

Similarly, more than one scholar has reported consensus on the prohibition of riba al-fadl (usury of excess) between each of the six mentioned types. Excess is therefore not permitted between gold and gold, nor between silver and silver, nor between wheat and wheat, nor between barley and barley, nor between dates and dates, nor between salt and salt, even if given hand to hand.

The truth about which there is no doubt is the prohibition of riba al-fadl within a single type of the six mentioned categories. If it is said: it is established in al-Sahih (the Sahih of al-Bukhari) from Ibn Abbas, from Usamah ibn Zayd, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "There is no riba except in al-nasi'ah (deferred exchange)." And it is established in al-Sahih from Abu al-Minhal that he said: "I asked al-Bara' ibn Azib and Zayd ibn Arqam about al-sarf (currency exchange), and they said: We were traders during the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and we asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about al-sarf, and he said: 'Whatever is hand to hand, there is no harm in it, and whatever is deferred, there is not [permitted]'." The answer is in several respects.

The first: the intent of the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding the permissibility of excess and the prohibition of deferment in what Usamah, al-Bara', and Zayd related from him, is only in two differing types, as is shown by the sound narrations that explicitly state that this is the place of permissibility of excess, and that within a single type it is prohibited.

Al-Bayhaqi chose this answer in al-Sunan al-Kubra, for after he cited the hadith we mentioned a moment ago from al-Bara' ibn Azib and Zayd ibn Arqam, he said the following: "al-Bukhari related it in al-Sahih from Abu 'Asim, without mentioning Amir ibn Mus'ab, and he also took it from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jurayj, with the mention of Amir ibn Mus'ab. Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj also related it from Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Abu al-Minhal, who said: 'A partner of mine sold silver on deferred terms until the season or until the Hajj,' and he mentioned it [in similar wording]. Al-Bukhari also related it, with a similar meaning, from 'Ali ibn al-Madini, from Sufyan, and likewise Ahmad ibn Rawh related it from Sufyan. It is also reported from al-Humaydi, from Sufyan, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Abu al-Minhal, who said: 'A partner of mine in Kufa sold dirhams for dirhams between them with an excess.'"

"In my view this is an error. The correct version is what 'Ali ibn al-Madini and Muhammad ibn Hatim related, and it is what is intended by what was stated without qualification in the narration of Ibn Jurayj. Thus the report refers to the sale of two types, one for the other, and he said: 'Whatever is hand to hand, there is no harm in it, and whatever is deferred, [it is not permitted].' This is what is intended by the hadith of Usamah. And God knows best."

What also indicates this is what Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Qattan informed us of in Baghdad: Abu Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Qattan told us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Birti told us: Abu 'Umar told us: Shu'bah told us: Habib, who is Ibn Abi Thabit, informed me, who said: "I heard Abu al-Minhal say: I asked al-Bara' and Zayd ibn Arqam about al-sarf, and both of them said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade the sale of silver for gold on credit." Al-Bukhari related it in al-Sahih from Abu 'Umar Hafs ibn 'Umar, and Muslim related it through another chain from Shu'bah. End of al-Bayhaqi's words verbatim. This is very clear regarding what we mentioned: that the intended permission of the mentioned excess is that it is in two types, not one type.

In Takmilat al-Majmu' (the supplement to al-Majmu'), after citing the passage from al-Bayhaqi that we mentioned, it says the following: "There is no proof for the one who relies on them both, because it is possible to interpret that on one of two matters. Either the intent is the sale of dirhams for something that is not a ribawi item, and the invalidity is due to the deferment until the season or the Hajj, which is not precisely defined, especially according to what the Arabs used to do.

The second: that it be interpreted as a difference of type, and another narration supports this: 'from Abu al-Minhal, who said: I asked al-Bara' ibn Azib and Zayd ibn Arqam about al-sarf, and both of them said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade the sale of gold for silver on credit.' Al-Bukhari and Muslim related it, and this is the wording of al-Bukhari and Muslim with a similar meaning. In Muslim's wording: 'the sale of silver for gold on credit,' which clarifies that the intent is the exchange of one type for another type."

This narration is established from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu al-Minhal. The three earlier narrations, the narration of al-Humaydi, and the two in al-Sahih, all their chains are of the utmost soundness.

(p-163) However, there is disagreement concerning Sufyan. al-Humaydi differed from 'Ali ibn al-Madini, Muhammad ibn Hatim, and Muhammad ibn Mansur, and each of al-Humaydi and 'Ali ibn al-Madini is of the utmost reliability. Ibn al-Madini is preferred here due to the corroboration of Muhammad ibn Hatim and Muhammad ibn Mansur for him, the testimony of Ibn Jurayj to his narration, and the testimony of Habib ibn Abi Thabit's narration to the narration of his teacher. For this reason al-Bayhaqi, may God have mercy on him, said: "The narration of the one who said he sold dirhams for dirhams is in error in his view." End of his words verbatim.

Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari the following: "al-Tabari said the meaning of the hadith of Usamah, 'There is no riba except in al-nasi'ah,' is when the types of sale differ." End of the point of relevance verbatim, and it agrees with what has been mentioned. He also said in Fath al-Bari, the following:

* *

Note

In the copy of al-Saghani, there occurs here: Abu 'Abd Allah said, meaning al-Bukhari: I heard Sulayman ibn Harb say: "There is no riba except in al-nasi'ah. This, according to us, is regarding gold for silver, and wheat for barley, in unequal amounts, and there is no harm in it hand to hand, but there is no good in it on credit." I say: This agrees. End of his words verbatim.

In the margin of the copy it is noted that after his saying "This agrees" there is a blank space in the original. From this answer that we mentioned, you know that the hadith of al-Bara' and Zayd does not need anything after this answer, because it is established in al-Sahih from them both that they explicitly state the difference of type, and thus the difficulty is resolved, and narrations explain one another. If it is said: this is not sufficient to rule that the narration established in al-Sahih permitting excess between dirhams and dirhams is an error, since one may say there is no contradiction between the mentioned narrations. Some of them state the exchange without qualification, and some of them clarify that they are dirhams for dirhams. So the unqualified is interpreted by the qualified, to reconcile the two narrations, since one of them clarified what the other left ambiguous. The hadith of Habib ibn Abi Thabit would be another hadith, relating to two types, and the prohibition of deferment in both, and there is no conflict or contradiction in that.

The answer, granting this, is in two matters. The first: that the permissibility of riba al-fadl has been abrogated (naskh).

The second: that the hadiths prohibiting riba al-fadl are more weighty and more worthy of consideration, on the assumption that there is no abrogation, than the hadiths permitting it.

(p-164) Among what indicates abrogation is what is established in al-Sahih from Abu al-Minhal, who said: "A partner of mine sold silver on deferred terms until the season or until the Hajj. He came to me and informed me, and I said: This is a matter that is not valid. He said: I have sold it in the market and no one objected to me. So I went to al-Bara' ibn Azib and asked him, and he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina while we were engaged in this kind of sale, and he said: 'What is hand to hand, there is no harm in it, and what is deferred is riba.' I then went to Zayd ibn Arqam, for he was greater in trade than I, and I asked him, and he said the same." This is the wording of Muslim in his Sahih. In it there is an explicit statement that the permission of the mentioned riba al-fadl in the hadith of al-Bara' ibn Azib and Zayd ibn Arqam coincided with the arrival of the Prophet (ﷺ) in Medina as an emigrant.

In some authentic reports concerning the prohibition of riba al-fadl (excess riba, i.e. unequal exchange of the same kind of commodity), he (ﷺ) declared its prohibition on the day of Khaybar (a Jewish oasis region taken by the Muslims in 7 AH). In some authentic reports the prohibition of riba al-fadl is also stated to have come after the conquest of Khaybar. It is established in the Sahih (the authentic collection) from the hadith of Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was at Khaybar, was brought a necklace containing beads and gold, and it was among the spoils being sold. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that the gold in the necklace be removed by itself, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: 'Gold for gold, weight for weight.'" This is the wording of Muslim in his Sahih. In another wording of his, also in his Sahih: "From Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, who said: I bought on the day of Khaybar a necklace for twelve dinars, containing gold and beads, so I separated them, and I found in them more than twelve dinars. I mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'It is not to be sold until it is separated.'" In another wording of his, also in his Sahih: "From Fadalah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Khaybar, exchanging gold for two or three dinars with the Jews, the ounce of gold. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do not sell gold for gold except weight for weight.'" It is also established in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man of the Banu 'Adi al-Ansari and appointed him over Khaybar, and he came with Janib dates (a superior type of dates), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Are all the dates of Khaybar like this?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), we buy a sa' (a measure) of it for two sa's of the mixed dates." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not do that; rather, equal for equal, or sell this and buy with its price from that. Likewise with the scale." This is the wording of Muslim in his Sahih. In another wording of theirs (Bukhari and Muslim), from Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id as well: "That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed a man over Khaybar, and he came with Janib dates, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'Are all the dates of Khaybar like this?' He said: 'No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we take a sa' of this for two sa's, and two sa's for three.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do not do that. Sell the mixed dates for dirhams, then buy Janib dates with the dirhams.'" Hadiths of this kind are many, and they are a clear text stating his (ﷺ) explicit declaration of the prohibition of riba al-fadl after the conquest of Khaybar. From these reports established in the Sahih it has become clear to you that the permission of riba al-fadl was at the time of his (ﷺ) arrival in Madinah as an emigrant, and that the reports explicitly stating the prohibition stated it on the day of Khaybar and after it. So the explicit declaration of the Prophet (ﷺ) of the prohibition of riba al-fadl after his arrival in Madinah by about six years or more indicates, without any ambiguity, abrogation (naskh). In any case, what matters is the later ruling, and the Companions used to act on the latest and then the newer.

Also, al-Bara' and Zayd (may Allah be pleased with them both) were not of age at the time they received the aforementioned hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), unlike the group of Companions who narrated from him the prohibition of riba al-fadl; for they were adults at the time of receiving. The narration of one who is adult at the time of receiving is stronger than the narration of one who received while a child, because there is disagreement about the latter, but not about one who received as an adult. The age of al-Bara' and Zayd at the time of his (ﷺ) arrival in Madinah was about ten years, according to what Ibn 'Abd al-Barr mentioned from Mansur ibn Salamah al-Khuza'i: that he narrated with his chain to Zayd ibn Harithah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarded him as too young on the day of Uhud, along with al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, Zayd ibn Arqam, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Sa'd ibn Habtah, and 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar. And from al-Waqidi, that the first battle they witnessed was the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq).

Among those who said that the hadith of al-Bara' and Zayd is abrogated is its narrator al-Humaydi. Enough for you is his knowledge and erudition. The statement of a narrator of a hadith that it is abrogated, regarding whether that suffices for abrogation, is a well-known disagreement among the scholars of usul al-fiqh (the principles of jurisprudence), and most of the Malikis and Shafi'is do not consider it sufficient. If it is said: what you have presented, that the prohibition of riba al-fadl came after its permission, indicates abrogation in the hadith of al-Bara' and Zayd, because of the knowledge of the chronology regarding them, and that the hadith of the prohibition is the later one; but where do you have knowledge of that in the hadith of Usamah? The birth of Usamah is close to the births of al-Bara' and Zayd, because Usamah's age at the time of the Prophet's (ﷺ) death was twenty years, and it is said eighteen; and the age of al-Bara' and Zayd at the time of his (ﷺ) death was about twenty, as we have already presented what indicates this.

The answer: it suffices for abrogation to know that the permission of riba al-fadl occurred before its prohibition, and the later ruling takes precedence over the earlier one.

The second answer: regarding the hadith of Usamah, it is the narration of a single Companion, while the reports prohibiting riba al-fadl come from a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who narrated them explicitly from him (ﷺ), clearly stating the prohibition of riba al-fadl. Among them are: Abu Sa'id, Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, Abu Hurayrah, Hisham ibn 'Amir, Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, Abu Bakrah, Ibn 'Umar, Abu al-Darda', Bilal, 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, (p-166) Ma'mar ibn 'Abdullah, and others. The reports of most of those we have mentioned are established in the Sahih, such as the reports of Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abu Bakrah, 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Ma'mar ibn 'Abdullah, and others. When you know this, the narration of a group of trustworthy narrators is stronger, more established, and further from error than the narration of a single one.

It has been established in the principles of jurisprudence that the multiplicity of narrators is one of the factors giving preference, and likewise the multiplicity of evidences, as al-Shinqiti's source Marāqi al-Su'ud stated in the section on preference (tarjih), regarding the status of what is transmitted, with his saying, in rajaz meter:

"And the multiplicity of evidence and of narration is a preferring factor for those of insight."

The view that multiplicity does not give preference is weak. Sulaym al-Dari mentioned that al-Shafi'i alluded to it, and some Shafi'is and Hanafis went to it.

The third answer: regarding the hadith of Usamah, it indicates the permission of riba al-fadl, while the hadiths of the group mentioned indicate its prohibition in the same kind of the mentioned commodities. It has been established in the principles of jurisprudence that a text indicating prohibition takes precedence over one indicating permission, because abandoning what is permissible is less severe than committing what is forbidden. We have already quoted this from the author of Marāqi, and this is the truth, contrary to al-Ghazali, 'Isa ibn Aban, Abu Hashim, and a group of the theologians, who said: the two are equal.

The fourth answer: regarding the hadith of Usamah, it is general in its apparent meaning, covering one kind and two kinds, while the hadiths of the group are more specific than it, because they explicitly state prohibition with the unity of the kind and permission with the difference of kinds. The more specific takes precedence over the more general, because it explains it, and a general and a specific do not conflict, as is established in the principles of jurisprudence. Among the factors preferring the hadiths prohibiting riba al-fadl over the hadith of Usamah is memorization, for among its narrators are Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, and others, who are well known for memorization. And there are other factors besides this.

Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (the commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari), and this is his text: "The scholars agreed on the authenticity of the hadith of Usamah, and they differed on reconciling it with the hadith of Abu Sa'id. It was said: it is abrogated, but abrogation is not established by possibility. It was said: the meaning of his saying 'there is no riba' is the riba that is more severe and strongly forbidden, the one threatened with severe punishment, as the Arabs say: there is no scholar in the town except Zayd, although there are other scholars besides him; the intention is negating the most complete, not negating the basic existence. Also, the negation of the prohibition of riba al-fadl from the hadith of Usamah is only by implication (mafhum), so the hadith of Abu Sa'id takes precedence over it, because its indication is by explicit statement (manțuq)."

(p-167) "And the hadith of Usamah is interpreted as referring to the greater riba, as was previously mentioned. And Allah knows best." End of quotation from him.

His statement "abrogation is not established by possibility" is rejected by what we have already presented of the reports explicitly stating that the prohibition after the permission, together with knowledge of the later one, is sufficient to indicate abrogation. It has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar that they both retracted from the view of permitting riba al-fadl. Al-Bayhaqi said in al-Sunan al-Kubra, and this is his text: "Chapter on what is used as evidence for the retraction of those from the early generation who said there is no riba except in deferment (nasi'ah) from their view and their abandoning it." Abu 'Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us: Abu al-Fadl ibn Ibrahim informed us: Ahmad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Abd al-A'la informed us: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, who said: "I asked Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas about exchange (sarf), and they saw no harm in it. While I was sitting with Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, I asked him about exchange, and he said: 'Whatever is in excess is riba.' I denied that, because of their statement, and he said: 'I will not narrate to you except what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): a man came to him with a sa' of good dates, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) dates were the inferior kind. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "From where do you have this?" He said: "I went with two sa's and bought with them this sa', for the price of this in the market is such, and the price of that in the market is such." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Have you engaged in riba? When you want that, sell your dates for goods, then buy with your goods whatever dates you wish."' Abu Sa'id said: 'Dates for dates are more deserving of being riba, or silver for silver?' He said: 'Then I came to Ibn 'Umar later, and he forbade me, and I did not come to Ibn 'Abbas.' He said: 'Abu al-Sahba' narrated to me that he asked Ibn 'Abbas, and he disliked it.'" Narrated by Muslim in the Sahih from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and he said: "And the dates of the Prophet (ﷺ) were of this color."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn Abu 'Ali al-Masarjisi narrated to us: my grandfather Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who is the son of the daughter of al-Hasan ibn 'Isa, narrated to us: my grandfather al-Hasan ibn 'Isa narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us: Ya'qub ibn Abi al-Qa'qa' informed us, from Ma'ruf ibn Sa'd, that he heard Abu al-Jawza' say: "I served Ibn 'Abbas for nine years when a man came and asked him about a dirham for two dirhams. Ibn 'Abbas cried out and said: 'This man is ordering me to feed him riba.' Some people around him said: 'If we were acting on your fatwa, we would be doing this.' Ibn 'Abbas said: 'I used to issue fatwas with that until Abu Sa'id and Ibn 'Umar related to me that the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade it, so I forbid you from it.'" In our copy of the Sunan of al-Bayhaqi, in this chain, it is "Ibn al-Mubarak," and the apparent correct reading is "Abu al-Mubarak," as will come.

Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Qattan informed us in Baghdad: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Durustawayh narrated to us (p-168): Ya'qub ibn Sufyan narrated to us: 'Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'd ibn Iyas, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: that a man from the Banu Shamakh ibn Fazarah asked him about a man who married a woman and saw her mother and was attracted to her, so he divorced his wife in order to marry her mother. He said: "There is no harm," so the man married her. 'Abdullah was in charge of the public treasury (bayt al-mal), and he used to sell the refuse of the public treasury, giving much and taking little, until he came to Madinah and asked the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they said: "It is not lawful for this man to have this woman, and silver is not valid except weight for weight." When 'Abdullah came, he went to the man but did not find him, and he found his people, and said: "The one you gave a fatwa to, your companion, is not lawful." They said: "She has already borne him children." He said: "Even if she has." He went to the money-changers and said: "O company of money-changers, what I used to sell to you is not lawful. Silver for silver is not lawful except weight for weight." End of al-Bayhaqi's quotation in his wording. In it is explicit evidence of the retraction of Ibn 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Mas'ud from the view of permitting riba al-fadl.

Ibn Hajar said, in his discussion of the hadith of Usama mentioned above, the following: "Ibn Umar opposed this view, meaning the view that forbids riba al-fadl (the excess in a sale of like goods). He later retracted it. Ibn Abbas also opposed it, though there is disagreement about whether he retracted. Al-Hakim narrated through the chain of Hayyan al-Adawi (with a non-dotted h and a dotted-underneath y, as in the vocalization of his name) that he asked Abu Mijlaz about al-sarf (the exchange of currencies), and he said: 'Ibn Abbas did not see any harm in it for a period of his life, as long as it was ayn bi-ayn, yadan bi-yad (hand to hand, of the same kind, at the same time). He used to say: Riba is only in al-nasi'a (deferred payment).' Then Abu Sa'id met him and mentioned the story and the hadith, in which there is: 'Dates for dates, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, gold for gold, silver for silver, hand to hand, like for like. Whatever exceeds is riba.' Ibn Abbas said: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.' After that, he used to forbid it most strongly." End of quote from Fath al-Bari, in its wording.

In Takmilat al-Majmu' by Taqi al-Din al-Subki, after citing this hadith of Hayyan, he said the following: "Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak and said: 'This is a hadith whose isnad is sahih, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not narrate it with this wording.' However, there is a question about his judgment that it is sahih. Hayyan ibn Ubayd Allah, the one mentioned, was described by Ibn Adi: 'Most of what he narrates consists of solitary reports (ifradat) which he alone transmits.' Ibn Adi also mentioned in his biography this hadith on al-sarf with its full wording, then said: 'This hadith is from the hadith of Abu Mijlaz from Ibn Abbas, transmitted solely by Hayyan.' Al-Bayhaqi said: 'The scholars have spoken about Hayyan.' Know that this hadith deserves attention, and that its soundness must be distinguished from its weakness, for a matter other than what we are discussing, namely his saying: 'And likewise for what is measured by volume or weight.' It has been criticized in two ways. One is the weakening of the hadith entirely, to which al-Bayhaqi pointed. (p-169) Among those who held this view is Ibn Hazm, who gave a reason for its weakness that I shall point out, so that no one is deceived by it. He gave three reasons:

The first: it is mursal (disconnected), because Abu Mijlaz did not hear from Abu Sa'id or from Ibn Abbas.

The second: because it mentions that Ibn Abbas retracted, and Ibn Hazm believed that this is false, since it contradicts Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The third: that Hayyan ibn Ubayd Allah is unknown (majhul).

As for his statement that it is mursal, it is not acceptable, because Abu Mijlaz met Ibn Abbas and heard from him, and he met Abu Sa'id. Once this is established, a claim of non-hearing is not accepted without proof. As for the contradiction with Sa'id ibn Jubayr, we will discuss it in this section, if Allah the Exalted wills. As for his statement that Hayyan ibn Ubayd Allah is unknown: if he meant unknown in identity (majhul al-'ayn), this is not correct. Rather, he is a well-known man. Muhammad ibn Ubada narrated this hadith on al-sarf from him, and al-Hakim narrated it through him. Ibn Hazm also mentioned him. Ibrahim ibn al-Hajjaj al-Shami narrated from him, and Ibn Adi narrated through him. Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated from him, and al-Bayhaqi narrated through him. He is Hayyan ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Hayyan ibn Bishr ibn Adi, a Basran who heard from Abu Mijlaz, Lahiq ibn Humayd, and al-Dahhak, and from his father. He narrated from Ata' and Ibn Buraydah. Musa ibn Isma'il, Muslim ibn Ibrahim, Abu Dawud, and Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated from him. Al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim each devoted an entry to him, and each mentioned some of what I have mentioned. He also has an entry in the book of Ibn Adi, as I have indicated. Thus the unknown identity is removed from him. If he meant unknown in condition (majhul al-hal), then he narrated it through the chain of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. He said in its isnad: 'Rawh informed us, saying: Hayyan ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to us, and he was a man of truthfulness (rajul sidq).' If this testimony to his truthfulness came from Rawh ibn Ubada, then Rawh is a hadith scholar, raised in hadith, expert in it, an author agreed upon as a reliable authority, a Basran of the same city, and the one to whom testimony is given. His testimony for him is therefore accepted. If this statement is from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, then that suffices, and consider who it is whom Ishaq praises. Ibn Abi Hatim has mentioned this Hayyan ibn Ubayd Allah.

He also mentioned a group of well-known persons who narrated from him and from whom he narrated. He said that he asked his father about him, and he said: 'Saduq (truthful).' Then he said: 'And from Sulayman ibn Ali al-Rabi'i, from Abu al-Jawza' Aws ibn Abd Allah al-Rabi'i, who said: I heard him (meaning Ibn Abbas) commanding al-sarf, and this was reported from him. Then (p-170) I was informed that he retracted that. I met him in Mecca and said: It has reached me that you retracted. He said: Yes, that was merely an opinion of mine. This Abu Sa'id narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he forbade al-sarf. We have narrated it in Sunan Ibn Majah and Musnad Imam Ahmad, with an isnad whose narrators meet the conditions of the Two Sahihs, through Sulayman ibn Ali. Sulayman ibn Ali was narrated from by Muslim.'

Ibn Hazm said: 'He is unknown, and no one knows who he is.' But this is not accepted from him, for what has been made clear. Then he said: 'And from Abu al-Jawza', who said: I used to serve Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) for nine years.' Then he cited the hadith of Abu al-Jawza' from Ibn Abbas, which we previously mentioned from al-Bayhaqi. Then he said: 'Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra with an isnad containing Abu al-Mubarak, who is unknown.'

Then he said: 'And we have narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Nu'm, with a dammah on the nun and a sukun on the ayn: that Abu Sa'id al-Khudri met Ibn Abbas and testified to him, on the authority of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Gold for gold, silver for silver, like for like, whoever exceeds has engaged in riba." Ibn Abbas said: "I repent to Allah for what I used to issue as a legal opinion." Then he retracted.' Al-Tabarani narrated it with a sahih isnad. Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Nu'm is a Successor (tabi'i), a reliable narrator agreed upon, known for narrating from Abu Sa'id, Ibn Umar, and other Companions.

And from Abu al-Jawza', who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about al-sarf, of a dirham for two dirhams, hand to hand. He said: 'I see no harm in what is hand to hand.' Then I came to Mecca the following year, and he had forbidden it. Al-Tabarani narrated it with a hasan isnad.

And from Abu al-Sha'tha', who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: 'O Allah, I repent to You from al-sarf. It is merely my opinion. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrates it from the Prophet (ﷺ).' Al-Tabarani narrated it, and its narrators are reliable, well known, and explicitly state the transmission in every link from the first to the last.

From Atiyya al-Awfi, with a sukun on the waw and with a fa': he said: Abu Sa'id said to Ibn Abbas: 'Repent to Allah the Exalted.' He said: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him.' He said: 'Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade gold for gold and silver for silver,' and he said: 'Indeed, I fear for you riba.' Fudayl ibn Marzuq said: I asked Atiyya: 'What is riba?' He said: 'The increase and the excess between them.' Al-Tabarani narrated it with a sahih chain up to Atiyya. Atiyya is among the narrators of the Sunan. Yahya ibn Ma'in said: 'Salih (righteous),' and others weakened him, so the isnad because of him is not strong.

And from Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani: that Ibn Abbas came from Medina to Mecca and I came with him. He praised Allah the Exalted and extolled Him, then said: 'O people, there is no harm in al-sarf, as long as it is hand to hand. Riba is only in al-nasi'a (deferred payment).' His saying spread among the people of the East and the West. When the season (al-mawsim) ended, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri came to him and said: 'O son of Abbas, have you eaten riba and fed it to others?' He said: 'Did I do that?!' He said: 'Yes.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: '(p-171) Gold for gold, by weight for weight, like for like, its unworked form and its coined form. Whoever exceeds or seeks more has engaged in riba. Barley for barley, dates for dates, salt for salt, like for like. Whoever exceeds or seeks more has engaged in riba.' When the following year came, Ibn Abbas came and I came with him. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people, "I spoke last year with a word from my own opinion, and I seek forgiveness from Allah the Exalted for it and repent to Him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Gold for gold, by weight for weight, like for like, its unworked form and its coined form. Whoever exceeds or seeks more has engaged in riba.'"' He repeated these six types to them." Al-Tabarani narrated it with an isnad containing an unknown narrator. We mention it only as a supporting corroboration (mutaba'a) for what came before. Thus it occurs in our narration: 'Whoever exceeds or seeks more' with the conjunction waw, not with aw (or). And Allah knows best.

Abu Jabir Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Salama al-Tahawi narrated in his book al-Ma'ani wa'l-athar, with a hasan isnad, from Abu Sa'id, who said: 'I said to Ibn Abbas: What do you say about the one who says, "a dinar for a dinar"?' And he mentioned the hadith. Then he said: Abu Sa'id said: Ibn Abbas withdrew from it. Al-Tahawi also narrated from Nasr ibn Marzuq, with an isnad that is not problematic, from Abu al-Sahba': that Ibn Abbas dropped the view on al-sarf. This is more explicit than the narration of Muslim. Al-Tahawi also narrated from Abu Umayya, with a hasan isnad, through Abd Allah ibn Husayn, that a man from the people of Iraq said to Abd Allah ibn Umar: 'Ibn Abbas said, while he was our governor: Whoever gives a hundred dirhams for a dirham, let him take it.' And he mentioned a hadith until he said: It was said to Ibn Abbas: 'What did Ibn Umar say?' He said: He sought forgiveness from his Lord and said: 'It is merely an opinion from me.'

And from Abu Hashim al-Wasiti, whose name is Yahya ibn Dinar, from Ziyad, who said: 'I was with Ibn Abbas in al-Ta'if, and he retracted from al-sarf seventy days before he died.' Ibn Abd al-Barr mentioned it in al-Istidhkar. He also mentioned from Abu Hurra, who said: A man asked Ibn Sirin about something, and he said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' The man said: 'Even if it is your opinion.' He said: 'I dislike to say something by my opinion, then another view appears to me and I seek you and cannot find you. Ibn Abbas held an opinion on al-sarf, then retracted.' It was also mentioned from Ibn Sirin, from al-Hudhayl, with a dhal (dotted) — the son of the sister of Muhammad ibn Sirin — who said: 'I asked Ibn Abbas about al-sarf, and he retracted from it. I said: The people say...' He said: 'The people may say whatever they wish.'" End of quote from Takmilat al-Majmu'. Then after this he said: "So these are numerous sahih and hasan narrations, through a group of Ibn Abbas's companions, indicating his retraction. Other reports of his retraction have also been transmitted, but what I have mentioned is sufficient, if Allah the Exalted wills."

Also in Takmilat al-Majmu', before this, is the following: "It was narrated (p-172) from Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki, whose name is Muhammad ibn Tadrus (with a fatha on the ta', a sukun on the dal, a dammah on the ra', and an undotted sin), who said: 'I heard Abu Usayd al-Sa'idi and Ibn Abbas giving a legal opinion (yuftii) that a dinar may be exchanged for two dinars.' Abu Usayd al-Sa'idi said to him, harshly: 'I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A dinar for a dinar, a sa' of wheat for a sa' of wheat, a sa' of barley for a sa' of barley, and a sa' of salt for a sa' of salt, with no excess between them in any of that."' Ibn Abbas said: 'This is merely something I used to say by my opinion, and I did not hear anything about it.'" Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak and said: "It is sahih according to the condition of Muslim (may Allah have mercy on him)." In its isnad is Ateeq ibn Ya'qub al-Zubayri. Al-Hakim said: "He is an elderly Qurashi from the people of Medina." And Abu Usayd is with a dammah on the hamza.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 276 (part 4 of 6):

It is related in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani, from the hadith of Abu Salih Dhakwan, that he asked Ibn 'Abbas about the sale of gold and silver. He said: "It is permissible with an excess or a deficiency, provided it is hand to hand." Abu Salih said: "So I asked Abu Sa'id (al-Khudri) about what Ibn 'Abbas had said, and I informed Ibn 'Abbas of what Abu Sa'id had said. They met, and I was with them. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri began by saying: 'O Ibn 'Abbas, what is this legal opinion (fatwa) that you give people concerning the sale of gold and silver, ordering them to exchange it with a deficiency or an excess, hand to hand?' Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: 'I am not the earliest of you in companionship with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and here are Zayd ibn Arqam and al-Bara' ibn 'Azib saying: We heard the Prophet ﷺ...'" Al-Tabarani related it with a hasan chain. We have already mentioned the retraction of Ibn 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud from this view, and we have already given the answer to what has been reported from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, Zayd ibn Arqam and Usama ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them all. And it is established from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that Ibn 'Abbas did not retract; but that is testimony to an absolute negation, and affirmation takes precedence over negation, because the one who affirms has knowledge of what the one who negates did not have knowledge of. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: "Whether Ibn 'Abbas retracted or did not retract, the Sunnah is sufficient in place of the statement of anyone; whoever opposes it is returned to it." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Refer ignorance back to the Sunnah." End of quotation.

And the eminent scholar al-Shawkani, may Allah have mercy on him, said in Nayl al-Awtar, in his exact words: As for what Muslim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that there is no riba in what is hand to hand, as mentioned earlier, that is not related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ such that its indication of the negation of riba al-fadl would be explicit. Even if it were marfu', Ibn 'Abbas would not have retracted and sought forgiveness when Abu Sa'id narrated that to him, as mentioned earlier. Al-Hazimi related Ibn 'Abbas's retraction and his seeking forgiveness when he heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and his son 'Abd Allah narrating from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what indicates the prohibition of riba al-fadl, and he said: "You two have memorized from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what I did not memorize." Al-Hazimi also related from him that he said: "That was by my own opinion." And here is Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrating to me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so I left my opinion for the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Even if we concede that what Ibn 'Abbas said is marfu', it is general and specified by the hadiths of the chapter, since they are more specific than it absolutely. End of quotation in his exact words. Many have mentioned that consensus was formed after this disagreement on the prohibition of riba al-fadl.

He said in Takmilat al-Majmu', in his exact words: The third section concerns the end of the disagreement on this matter and the claim of consensus regarding it. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The scholars of the major cities agreed: Malik ibn Anas and those who followed him among the people of Madina, Sufyan al-Thawri and those who agreed with him among the people of Iraq, al-Awza'i and those who said his view among the people of Syria, al-Layth ibn Sa'd and those who agreed with him among the people of Egypt, al-Shafi'i and his companions, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, al-Nu'man, Ya'qub and Muhammad ibn 'Ali, that it is not permissible to sell gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, or salt for salt, with excess, hand to hand, or on credit (nasi'ah); and that whoever does so has committed riba, and the sale is void. End of quotation; the point of the matter in his exact words.

Al-Nawawi, in Sharh Muslim, reported the consensus of the Muslims on abandoning the apparent meaning of the hadith of Usama. He said: This indicates its abrogation. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr argued for the soundness of its interpretation of the hadith of Usama by the consensus of the people, except Ibn 'Abbas on it. End of quotation. And even if we suppose that Ibn 'Abbas did not retract from this, can consensus be formed with his dissent? There is a well-known disagreement in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) on this: does the dissent of one or two negate consensus, or must there be agreement of all, which is the well-known view? And if one who dissented died, and consensus was then formed after him, does that count as consensus? This is the apparent view; or does it not count as consensus, because the dissent of a deceased dissenter does not lapse by his death? This is also a well-known disagreement in the principles.

* *

Once you know that the one who held the permissibility of riba al-fadl retracted from it, and you know that the sound hadiths agreed upon explicitly and abundantly prohibit it, you know that the truth beyond doubt is the prohibition of riba al-fadl between each single kind of the six (items) with itself, and the permissibility of excess between two differing kinds hand to hand, and the prohibition of deferred exchange (nasa') between gold and silver absolutely, and between dates and wheat, and between barley and salt absolutely; and food is not prohibited for money on credit, and vice versa. Some scholars related consensus on this. What remains outside these six categories stated in the hadith: the majority of scholars hold that riba is not restricted to the six mentioned.

The verified position is that the effective cause (illah) of riba in the two precious metals is that they are both precious substances, the prices of things generally in all regions of the world. This is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i, and the cause in them is confined to them according to them. The best-known narration from Ahmad is that the cause in them is that each of them is a measured (mawzun) genus. This is the position of Abu Hanifa. As for wheat, barley, dates and salt, the cause of riba in them according to Malik is being staple food (iqtiyat) and storable (idikhar), and it has been said also prevalence as a staple of life. Riba al-fadl is therefore not prohibited according to Malik and the general body of his companions except in gold for gold and silver for silver, and staple storable food for staple storable food. It has been said that along with being staple and storable, prevalence as a staple of life is required. Malik made the cause what he mentioned because it is the most specific of the attributes of the four mentioned. Some Malikis versified what involves riba of deferment and riba of excess according to Malik in two verses, which are: [Tawil]

"The riba of deferment in currency is forbidden, and likewise food, even if the two kinds are multiple."
"Riba of excess is restricted to currency, and likewise food, the riba of which applies if the kind of each is unified."

I had previously set out Malik's position on this in my lengthy verses on the branches of Malik's school, in discussing riba in foods, with my words: [Rajaz]

"Every food that is tasted: deferred riba in it is among the forbidden,
Whether staple, storable, or neither; it differs, and that food's kind is one or varied."
"If it is used for medicine
Alone, then prohibition is absent."
"And riba al-fadl has conditions by which it is forbidden,
And with their absence it ceases:
They are unity of the kind in what has been mentioned,
Together with its being a staple, and that it be storable."
"And what sets the limit of storability as a period,
And the tadili (a particular term) with six, has limited it."
"The disagreement on requiring that it be a staple of life by custom,
And whoever dropped it took the position of dropping it."
"Its benefit appears in four: prevalence as a staple of life does not occur with them."
"The four contained in this verse: eggs, figs, locusts, oil."
"In eggs and oil riba is prohibited, for it is forbidden in consideration of the non-requirement of its condition."
"The requirement of its condition was observed in the Mukhtasar, in figs alone, so in it what is forbidden is found."
"A disagreement was observed regarding locusts, evident by its mention of disagreement concerning locusts."
"A single grain for two grains is forbidden, since riba's small amount is forbidden."

Then after that I mentioned the disagreement over whether eggs are subject to riba, with my words: [Rajaz]

"And the statement that eggs are not subject to riba is attributed to the imam Ibn Sha'ban."

The soundest narrations from al-Shafi'i are that the cause of riba in the four is taste (tu'm), so every food in which riba is prohibited according to him is like staple foods, condiments, sweets, fruits and medicines. He argued that the cause is taste from what Muslim narrated from the hadith of Ma'mar ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Food for food, like for like," the hadith. And "food" is the name for everything that is eaten. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:93), and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Let man look at his food﴾ ﴿That We poured water in torrents﴾ ﴿Then We split the earth in splitting﴾ ﴿And caused grain to grow therein﴾ ﴿And grapes and herbage﴾ (Abasa 80:24-28), and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The food of those given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:5), meaning their slaughtered animals.

'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "We remained with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a year, having no food except the two blacks: dates and water." And from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, in his lengthy hadith narrating his conversion to Islam, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Who used to feed you?" I said: "I had no food except the water of Zamzam, and I became so fat that the folds of my belly were broken." He said: "It is blessed; it is food of sustenance." Narrated by Muslim.

Labid said: [Kamil]

"For a dust-covered, tawny one, over whose carcass dusky, hunting (beasts) contend, whose food is not withheld."

By "its food" he means its prey. They said: The Prophet ﷺ attached riba in this hadith to the name "food," and a ruling attached to a derived name indicates that it is its effective cause, like cutting in theft in His saying: ﴿And the thief, male and female﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:38). They said: Because grain, as long as it is food, is subject to riba; when it is sown and ceases to be food, riba does not apply to it; when the grain forms and becomes food, riba applies to it. This shows that the cause in it is being food. For this reason water is subject to riba according to one of the two views among the Shafi'is, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed Allah will test you with a river; whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is of me﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:249), and because of 'A'isha's previously mentioned saying: "We had no food except the two blacks, water and dates," and because of the poet's words: [Tawil]

"If you wish, I will forbid women other than you, and if you wish, I will not give you cool, fresh water."

Nuqakh is cold water. This is the argument of the Shafi'is that the cause of riba in the four is taste, so they attached to them every food, by the common cause that unites them.

The author, may Allah pardon him, says: Using Ma'mar's hadith mentioned above to show that the cause of riba is taste is, in my view, open to examination, and Allah the Exalted knows best. For when Ma'mar, after saying: "I used to hear the Prophet ﷺ say: 'Food for food, like for like,'" added immediately: "And our food on that day was barley," as narrated from him by Ahmad and Muslim. This is explicit that "food" in their custom on that day was barley. It is established in the principles that a custom accompanying the address is one of the specifiers of a general text. Al-Marqi al-Su'ud expressed it in the section on the detached specifier, adding to what specifies generality: [Rajaz]

"Custom where it accompanies the address, and leave aside the pronoun of part and the causes."

The best-known narration from Ahmad is that the cause of riba in the four is that they are measured (makilat) kinds, which is the position of Abu Hanifa. Accordingly riba is prohibited in every measured item, even if not food, such as plaster, lime and soap-wort. They argued with what al-Daraqutni narrated from 'Ubadah and Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet ﷺ said: "What is weighed, like for like, when it is of one kind; and what is measured, likewise. But if the two kinds differ, there is no harm in it." Al-Shawkani said in Nayl al-Awtar: The hadith of Anas and 'Ubadah was pointed to by al-Talkhis, but it did not comment on it. Its chain includes al-Rabi' ibn Subayh, whom Abu Zur'ah and others declared reliable, while a group declared him weak. This hadith was also narrated by al-Bazzar, and the hadith of 'Ubadah mentioned earlier and other hadiths testify to its soundness. End of quotation in his exact words.

And they also cited what al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurayrah: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed a man over Khaybar, and he brought them dates of the finest quality (janīb). He said: 'Are all the dates of Khaybar like this?' He said: 'No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah. We take a ṣāʿ (a measure) of this for two ṣāʿs, and two ṣāʿs for three.' He said: 'Do not do that. Sell the mixed dates for dirhams, then buy with the dirhams finest dates (janīb).'" And he said: "In the scale (al-mīzān) there is the same." The point of argument from it is that his saying "in the scale" means "in what is weighed (al-mawzūn)," because the scale itself is not among the items of ribā.

They also cited the hadith of Abu Sa'id mentioned earlier, which al-Ḥākim narrated through the chain of Ḥayyān ibn ʿUbayd Allah, for in it the Prophet ﷺ said: "Dates for dates, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, gold for gold, silver for silver, hand to hand, equal for equal, like for like. Whoever gives more or takes more has committed ribā." Then he said: "And likewise whatever is measured by volume or by weight."

The proponents of the opposing view responded that the hadith of al-Dāraqutnī is not established, and likewise the hadith of al-Ḥākim. We have already explained earlier what indicates the authenticity of the hadith of Ḥayyān mentioned. We have also cited just now the statement of al-Shawkānī that the hadith of al-Dāraqutnī was also narrated by al-Bazzār, and that the hadith of ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit and others corroborates its soundness. Abu Zurʿah and others declared al-Rabīʿ ibn Ṣubayḥ trustworthy, while a group declared him weak, and Ibn Ḥajar said of him in al-Taqrīb: "Truthful, poor in memory, and he was a devout ascetic and a fighter (in the path of Allah)."

What al-Shawkānī meant by the hadith of ʿUbādah mentioned is what Muslim, Imam Aḥmad, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah and Abu Dāwud narrated from him: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, salt for salt, like for like, equal for equal, hand to hand. When these kinds differ, sell however you wish." End of quotation. His saying ﷺ "equal for equal, like for like" indicates the determination by measure and weight, and this view is the strongest of them in evidence.

They answered the hadith of Abu Sa'id, which is agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayh), with three answers:

First: The answer of al-Bayhaqī, who said: "It has been said that his saying 'and likewise the scale' is a statement of Abu Sa'id al-Khudrī and is mawqūf (ending with a companion)."

Second: The answer of al-Qāḍī Abu al-Ṭayyib and others, that the apparent meaning of the hadith is not intended, because the scale itself has no ribā in it, so you must supply "the weighed (mawzūn)." But the claim of generality in implied words (al-muḍmarāt) is not valid.

Third: Carrying "the weighed" upon gold and silver alone, in order to combine the evidences.

The apparent position is that these answers do not stand, because treating it as mawqūf on Abu Sa'id goes against the apparent meaning; the intent of "what is weighed" by his saying "and likewise the scale" is not ambiguous; and restricting "the weighed" to gold and silver alone goes against the apparent meaning. And Allah knows best.

Regarding the effective cause (ʿillah) of ribā in the four items, there are other doctrines besides what we mentioned from the four Imams and those who agree with them:

First: The doctrine of the people of the apparent meaning (Ahl al-Ẓāhir) and those who agree with them, that there is no ribā at all except in the six items. This view is narrated from Ṭāwūs, Masrūq, al-Shaʿbī, Qatādah and ʿUthmān al-Battī.

Second: The doctrine of Abu Bakr ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kaysān al-Aṣamm, that the effective cause in them is that the item is something from which one benefits. Al-Qāḍī Ḥusayn related this from him.

Third: The doctrine of Ibn Sīrīn and Abu Bakr al-Awdanī of the Shafiʿites, that the effective cause is the genus (al-jinsiyyah). Thus ribā is prohibited in everything sold for its own kind, such as dust for dust, a garment for two garments, a sheep for two sheep, with unequal exchange.

Fourth: The doctrine of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, that the effective cause is the benefit within the genus. So according to him it is permissible to sell a garment worth one dinar for two garments worth one dinar together, and it is prohibited to sell a garment worth one dinar for a garment worth two dinars.

Fifth: The doctrine of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that the effective cause is the closeness of benefit within the genus. So he prohibited unequal exchange of wheat for barley, of bāqilāʾ (broad beans) for chickpeas, and of millet (dukhn) for sorghum (dhurrah), equal for equal.

Sixth: The doctrine of Rabīʿah ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that the effective cause is that it is a genus in which zakāh is obligatory. So he prohibited ribā in every genus in which zakāh is obligatory, such as livestock, crops and others.

Seventh: The doctrine of Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and the old opinion (qawl al-qadīm) of al-Shāfiʿī: that the effective cause is that it is a food that is measured or weighed, and he negated it from anything else, which is everything that is neither eaten nor drunk, or is eaten but is not measured or weighed, such as quince (safarjal) and watermelon (biṭṭīkh).

We have left aside the citing of evidence for these doctrines and discussion of them, fearing a tedious lengthening.

* *

Branches (furūʿ)

First branch: Doubt about equality is like certainty of excess; it is prohibited in every item in which ribā al-faḍl (ribā of excess) is prohibited. The evidence for this is what Muslim and al-Nasāʾī narrated from Jābir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of a heap of dates (ṣabrah) whose measure is not known, for a specified measure of dates."

Second branch: It is not permissible to delay the taking of possession of items in which ribā al-nasīʾah (ribā of deferment) is prohibited. The evidence for this is what al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Mālik ibn Aws, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I came, saying: 'Who will exchange dirhams?' Ṭalḥah said: 'Show us the gold until our treasurer comes, then come and take your silver.' ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'No! By Him in whose hand is my soul, you must either return his gold to him, or you must pay him his silver in full. For I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Gold for silver is ribā unless it is hand to hand (hā wa-hā); wheat for wheat is ribā unless it is hand to hand; barley for barley is ribā unless it is hand to hand; dates for dates is ribā unless it is hand to hand."'"

Third branch: It is not permissible to sell a ribawī item for another ribawī item when there is something else with one of them, such as gold for gold with something else added to one of them. The evidence for this is what Muslim narrated in his Ṣaḥīḥ, from Abu al-Ṭāhir, from Ibn Wahb, from the hadith of Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd al-Anṣārī, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought, while he was in Khaybar, a necklace containing beads and gold, and it was among the spoils of war being sold. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that the gold in the necklace be removed, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: 'Gold for gold, by weight for weight.'"

Muslim also narrated something similar from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd, from the hadith of Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd, may Allah be pleased with him, and similar to it. It was narrated by al-Nasāʾī, Abu Dāwud, and al-Tirmidhī, who graded it sound.

Al-ʿAllāmah al-Shawkānī, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said in Nayl al-Awṭār, when mentioning the author of al-Muntaqā, regarding the hadith of Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd mentioned: the hadith, with the following text.

In al-Talkhīṣ it is said: It has, in al-Ṭabarānī's al-Kabīr, very many chains. In some of them the necklace contains beads and gold; in some, gold and jewels; in some, beads hung on gold; in some, for twelve dinars; in some, for nine dinars; and in another, for seven dinars. Al-Bayhaqī answered this difference by saying that these were sales which Faḍālah witnessed.

The Ḥāfiẓ said: "The sound answer in my view is that this difference does not necessitate weakness. Rather, the purpose of the argument is preserved and free of disagreement, which is the prohibition of selling what has not been separated. As for its kind and the amount of its price, nothing related to it in this case requires a ruling of irregularity (iḍṭirāb). Then it is appropriate to weigh between its transmitters, and even if all are trustworthy, the narration of the most retentive and precise of them is to be judged sound, so the narrations of the rest relative to it are considered anomalous (shādhdhah). Some of these narrations that al-Ṭabarānī mentioned are in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and Sunan Abi Dāwud." End of quotation from him in his words. We have already mentioned some of Muslim's narrations.

Fourth branch: It is not permissible to sell worked gold or silver (al-maṣūgh) for the same kind in excess of its weight. The evidence for this is what is authentically reported from a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he ﷺ explicitly prohibited the sale of silver for silver and gold for gold except equal for equal, and that whoever gives more or asks for more has engaged in ribā.

Al-Bayhaqī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā narrated from Mujāhid that he said: "I was circumambulating with ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar when a goldsmith came to him and said: 'O Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, I work gold, then I sell some of it for more than its weight, and I take as a surplus the amount of the labor of my hands in it.' ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar forbade him from that, and the goldsmith kept repeating the question to him while ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar kept forbidding him, until he reached the door of the mosque, or his mount, intending to ride it."

Then ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar said: "The dinar for the dinar and the dirham for the dirham, with no excess between them. This is the covenant of our Prophet ﷺ to us, and our covenant to you."

Then al-Bayhaqī said: "The hadith of Muʿāwiyah has already passed, where he sold a vessel (siqāyah) of gold or silver for more than its weight, and Abu al-Dardāʾ forbade him, and what was related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, in forbidding that."

Al-Bayhaqī also narrated from Abu Rāfiʿ that he said: "I said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: 'I work gold, then I sell it by its weight and take a wage for the labor of my hand.' He said: 'Do not sell gold for gold except weight for weight, and silver for silver except weight for weight, and do not take any excess.'" End of quotation from him.
